summary: Sets the reading direction, left-to-right or right-to-left, for everything inside it. Components that depend on direction follow it with no extra wiring.

dir.note: The direction applied to the subtree. It is the native dir attribute, so text, flex rows and logical CSS properties all follow it.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.notes: sb-direction host: display: contents, so it adds no box. Its dir attribute does the work.

aria: the dir attribute is the platform's mechanism, so assistive technology and bidi text handling use it directly
components that need direction read it from the platform: :dir() in CSS, getComputedStyle(...).direction in the roving-focus controller (tabs arrows reverse in right-to-left)

useCases.when: A region whose language reads right to left inside a left-to-right page, or the reverse
Setting the direction of a whole page
useCases.use: dir on the html element is enough

antiPatterns.why: Text, focus order and logical properties stay in the old direction
antiPatterns.alternative: Use dir and logical CSS properties

coverage: dir reflects and sets subtree direction
sb-tabs roving focus reverses under rtl and flips back (also story starting in rtl)
tabs lay out from the right
pagination chevrons mirror only in rtl

drift.contract: native dir attribute on the host, read by components through :dir() and computed direction
drift.realization: the visual reference provides a React context; no context is needed in Web Components

openQuestions.question: Does sb-direction draw a box?
openQuestions.answer: No: display: contents, so it can wrap anything without changing layout.

openQuestions.question: How do other components learn the direction?
openQuestions.answer: From the platform (:dir(), computed direction), never from a context, so components work without sb-direction too.
